metadata.focus: Finish all 18 remaining original P0 alternate-source replacements with date/observation/independence caveats
metadata.notes: Completed 18 P0 story replacements with two date/event/location research links each and clear original observation/institutional dependency cautions. Detailed metrics, storm-total chronology, station metadata, graphics, and archival licenses still need publication-grade review. P1/P2 remain unverified.

alternate_reviews.title: Atmospheric-river rain triggers debris flows in Southern California burn scars
alternate_reviews.location: Silverado Canyon and the Bond Fire burn area, Orange County, California
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On January 28, 2021, rainfall from a Pacific atmospheric river triggered additional debris flows in the Bond Fire burn area near Silverado, Southern California.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: USGS mapped post-fire debris-flow impacts and WPC independently analyzed the regional atmospheric river; both rely on some common rain observations, and the California storm began January 26.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: USGS documents separate debris-flow episodes on January 25 and 28; do not place January 27 central-coast debris flows or multiday storm totals wholly on January 28. Avoid implying all burn scars responded the same way.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original January 28 hourly rainfall intensity and burned-slope cross-section with dated debris-flow observations.

alternate_reviews.title: A deadly avalanche buries part of Bingham Canyon, Utah
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On February 17, 1926, a major natural avalanche swept into Bingham Canyon, Utah, destroying homes and a boarding house following a snowy period.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: Utah Avalanche Center event entry and Utah Geological Survey historical hazard archive independently index the precise date/location but draw on overlapping period newspapers and avalanche historical compilations.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Historical fatality totals vary (35, 39 or about 40 depending on registry and retrospective accounts). Avoid an exact death figure until source/scope reconciled. Avalanche was snow, rock and debris, not only a simple snow slab.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original Bingham Canyon slope/settlement hazard map with documented avalanche runout and archive-source uncertainty.

alternate_reviews.title: An exceptional North Sea storm surge overtops defenses in Hamburg
alternate_reviews.location: Hamburg and the lower Elbe River, Germany
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: During the early morning of February 17, 1962, a devastating North Sea storm surge reached Hamburg and breached flood defenses along the lower Elbe; Hamburg's historic tide archive marks the local storm-tide peak around 03:08.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: Hamburg municipal tide/flood archives and NDR's event chronology cross-check the local date; NDR's reporting draws partly on municipal historical/meteorological records, so numerical claims require original gauge context.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Severe cyclone winds developed February 16 and surge flooding occurred overnight February 16–17; mark early February 17 local tide peak, not storm's initial formation. Gauge heights require correct elevation datum.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original Lower Elbe surge propagation and dated Hamburg tide-stage curve with levee breaches mapped.

alternate_reviews.title: A late-February blizzard paralyzes the New York metropolitan area
alternate_reviews.location: New York City, Long Island, southern Connecticut and northern New Jersey
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On February 23, 2026, a strong coastal cyclone generated heavy snow, damaging wind and qualifying blizzard conditions across numerous New York metropolitan counties.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS New York documents observed snow/blizzard criteria, while WPC independently reconstructs the same coastal low but uses shared NWS reports and analysis data; neither source clears claims of individual town storm totals.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Storm began February 22; confirm local blizzard-criteria timing and distinguish preliminarily confirmed county-wide reports from single-site sustained wind data. Final snowfall amounts cover multiple days.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original February 22–23 coastal cyclone track, snowband radar timeline and locally verified blizzard-observation map.

alternate_reviews.title: Fort McMurray wildfire emergency continues across northern Alberta
alternate_reviews.location: Fort McMurray and Wood Buffalo, Alberta, Canada
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On May 11, 2016, Alberta's emergency authorities maintained urgent fire-related restrictions and response measures around Fort McMurray while the long-running wildfire emergency continued.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: The Government of Alberta's contemporaneous May 11 alert directly documents ongoing operational restrictions; NASA JPL's May 11 publication documents earlier MISR observations, not a new May 11 satellite image.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The Fort McMurray fire started earlier in May; JPL article date was May 11 but its referenced MISR acquisition was May 6. Do not claim first ignition, initial evacuation or displayed satellite image occurred May 11.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original fire-growth versus dated public-alert timeline distinguishing May 6 MISR acquisition and May 11 Alberta bulletin.

alternate_reviews.title: Cyclone Yvette begins a devastating Balkan rainfall episode
alternate_reviews.location: Sava River basin and western Balkans
alternate_reviews.primary_publisher: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: University of Reading Weather and Climate
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On May 13, 2014, an intense, persistent precipitation episode associated with the developing Balkan cyclone Yvette began over the western Balkans, before catastrophic flooding developed over subsequent days.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: ECMWF's operational forecast/verification chronology and University of Reading meteorological reconstruction independently describe May 13 rainfall onset but share some ECMWF model and hydrometric datasets.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The worst flooding and major river peaks occurred May 14–18, not all on May 13; May 13 denotes beginning of the high-rainfall episode, not highest daily water stage. Different studies use May 13/14 analysis start.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original May 13–16 cutoff low track and 24-hour rain chart separating rain onset from later river crests.

alternate_reviews.title: A nocturnal EF1 tornado strikes Laguna Heights near South Padre Island
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Early May 13, 2023, a tornado rated EF1 struck Laguna Heights, Texas, producing extensive structural damage and a deadly local impact near South Padre Island.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS Brownsville case study presents survey/radar analysis while contemporaneous ABC reporting separately documents scene and human impacts, but EF1 intensity relies on the NWS survey.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The earlier selected Bayside, Texas NCEI segment is a different locale; do not transfer its reported path or damage counts. EF1 is a surveyed damage rating, not an observed 10-m wind speed. Injury and casualty figures vary by report release.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original May 13 radar/sea-breeze-boundary analysis, local tornado path, and damage survey indicators.

alternate_reviews.title: A derecho produces a rare Lake Michigan seiche
alternate_reviews.location: Chicago, Illinois and the southern Lake Michigan shoreline
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On July 11, 2011, fast-moving severe thunderstorm winds swept northern Illinois and southern Lake Michigan, damaging trees and structures and helping generate a lake seiche.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS Chicago details the local measured harbor water-level response while NOAA's derecho historical summary independently describes broad July 10–11 convective wind swaths, though both are NOAA analyses.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The derecho evolved July 10–11 across a multistate path; the lake seiche occurred July 11. Do not attribute 1,300+ miles of damage to a single Chicago thunderstorm line or misrepresent seiche as storm surge.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original July 11 convective radar bow echo paired with harbor water-level oscillation timeline.

alternate_reviews.title: A devastating hailstorm sweeps Colorado's Front Range
alternate_reviews.location: Denver and Colorado's Front Range, USA
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: University of Colorado Western Water Assessment
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On July 11, 1990, intense thunderstorms dropped destructive large hail along Colorado's Front Range, including the Denver area, causing an historically expensive hail disaster.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NWS historical reference and Colorado Western Water Assessment event catalog separately date the episode; impact costs trace to historical insurance and Storm Data compilations, not independent hail-gauge observations.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: A $600-million figure is an approximately 1990-era reported damage estimate, not an inflation-adjusted modern figure or current national rank. Hailstone maxima differ by location and reporting methodology.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original storm-track and hail-size reports across Denver with historical-versus-adjusted damages clearly distinguished.

alternate_reviews.title: Death Valley records an extraordinary 120°F midnight temperature
alternate_reviews.primary_publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: The Weather Channel historical heat reporting
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On July 17, 2023, Death Valley experienced a reported 120°F temperature around midnight during the exceptional July heat wave, as documented in NOAA's July 2023 national climate summary.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NOAA NCEI official monthly climate assessment and independent media reporting both cite a 120°F midnight reading, likely relying on the same underlying temperature record rather than independent instruments.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: The midnight observation is not July 17's afternoon maximum and is not the same as a daily minimum; site/time zone may differ between Badwater Basin and official Furnace Creek observations. Confirm station sensor and exact local clock prior to final X copy.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original July 16–17 hourly temperature curve highlighting midnight reading separately from daily maximum and minimum.

alternate_reviews.title: Hurricane Emily reaches Category 5 intensity over the Caribbean
alternate_reviews.location: Northwestern Caribbean Sea southwest of Jamaica
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: American Meteorological Society Monthly Weather Review
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Near 0000 UTC on July 17, 2005, Hurricane Emily was assessed at Category 5 intensity in the Caribbean after rapid strengthening, with the peak category documented in subsequent NHC analyses.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: NOAA Mariners Weather Log and the peer-reviewed Atlantic season analysis cross-reference common National Hurricane Center best-track and reconnaissance aircraft data; separate publications are not independent flight observations.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: 0000 UTC July 17 was still evening July 16 for some Caribbean local clocks. The 140-kt intensity is a poststorm best-track estimate, not a 10-meter anemometer measurement; later July 18–20 landfalls cannot be used as July 17 claims.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original UTC/local time comparison of Emily's central pressure, category/intensity and track near Jamaica.

alternate_reviews.title: Chicago logs an extraordinary daily rainfall record as Ike moisture surges north
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On September 13, 2008, Chicago O'Hare recorded 6.64 inches of rain in a day during a predecessor heavy-rain event enhanced by deep tropical moisture associated with Hurricane Ike.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: State climate analysis compiles the O'Hare observing record and NWS Chicago independently reconstructs the synoptic boundary/moisture transport, but both cite the same airport gauge and storm reports.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Much of the Chicago heavy rain preceded arrival of Ike's remnant circulation, as a quasi-stationary front and tropical moisture plume produced a predecessor rain event. Different stations and two-day accumulations vary; label O'Hare specifically.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original September 13 24-h O'Hare rain hyetograph and southwest-to-northeast moisture transport/front map.

alternate_reviews.title: Medicane Ianos drives major flood damage across central Greece
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On September 19, 2020, torrential rainfall and flash flooding associated with Medicane Ianos affected central Greece, especially Thessaly, after the cyclone reached the Ionian coast the day before.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: The EU Copernicus/JRC flood mapping inventory names September 19 as the Thessaly flooding episode, while NASA IMERG independently estimates the broader September 14–20 rain footprint using satellite algorithms.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Ianos reached western Greece on September 18, not September 19. NASA's rainfall graphic spans September 14–20; do not label storm-total rainfall as a September 19 one-day gauge amount. Flood mapping date is not landfall date.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original September 19 Thessaly catchment/flood footprint over annotated IMERG daily rainfall and track valid times.

alternate_reviews.title: A rare September EF3 tornado strikes western Wisconsin
alternate_reviews.location: Elk Mound–Wheaton corridor in Dunn and Chippewa Counties, Wisconsin
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: WEAU regional news and local emergency management
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On the evening of September 24, 2019, a tornado intensified to EF3 while moving from near Elk Mound into the Wheaton area of western Wisconsin.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: The NWS surveyed tornado damage and rating, while contemporaneous regional reporting independently documents extensive impacts but draws its final EF3 classification from that same NWS survey.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: EF3 damage was confined to portions of the track; the originally selected Albertville local record is not an independent separate rating or a whole-track EF3 wind measure. Verify tornado segments before final geometry.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original southeast Minnesota/western Wisconsin radar supercell and surveyed tornado track with EF3 indicators.

alternate_reviews.title: A nocturnal QLCS produces multiple Tennessee tornadoes
alternate_reviews.location: Middle Tennessee, including Rutherford, Coffee and Grundy Counties
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: Late November 5 into the early hours of November 6, 2018, a fast-moving quasi-linear convective system produced multiple tornadoes across Middle Tennessee.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: The NWS post-event survey documents QLCS morphology and eventual tornado path revisions; WSMV contemporaneously reported local damage and fatalities, drawing EF ratings from NWS.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Early preliminary reports listed a single long-track tornado, but 2019 satellite-based review identified two separate tornado paths in one corridor. Do not quote early counts or implied path continuity as definitive; anchor November 6 after midnight local.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original midnight-to-dawn QLCS reflectivity/velocity evolution and corrected separate track segmentation.

alternate_reviews.title: Intense overnight rainfall sends a violent flash flood through Mandra, Greece
alternate_reviews.location: Mandra and Nea Peramos, western Attica, Greece
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On the morning of November 15, 2017, extraordinary convective rain rapidly overwhelmed steep small catchments west of Athens, triggering destructive flash flooding in Mandra and Nea Peramos.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: Copernicus dated flood-response mapping and a separate peer-reviewed radar/rainfall-hydrology analysis independently establish event/date/location, but land impacts and death figures may derive from the same official response sources.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Rain began late on November 14 UTC while the most destructive flooding was early November 15 local. Death counts in provisional response updates and later studies differ (20, 23, 24). Do not publish an unqualified casualty figure; archive imagery has separate rights.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original November 14–15 convective rainfall and rapid runoff timeline for small Attica watersheds, using reproducible radar data.

alternate_reviews.title: Hurricane Kate rapidly deepens over the eastern Gulf of Mexico in November
alternate_reviews.location: Eastern Gulf of Mexico, southwest of Florida
alternate_reviews.primary_publisher: NOAA Weather Prediction Center tropical historical rainfall analysis
alternate_reviews.secondary_publisher: National Hurricane Center research in Monthly Weather Review
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On November 20, 1985, Hurricane Kate strengthened over the eastern Gulf of Mexico, with poststorm analysis documenting a pressure decline from approximately 972 hPa at 0000 UTC to 953 hPa near 2000 UTC.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: The WPC historical account and original NHC peer-reviewed annual cyclone summary both use NOAA reconnaissance and best-track analysis; they are complementary summaries of the same aircraft/buoy observations, not independent independent measurements.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Kate crossed the northern Cuban coast on November 19, intensified November 20 in the Gulf, and made Florida Panhandle landfall November 21. Do not describe the November 20 peak central pressure as an at-landfall observation or assume a buoy pressure equals exact cyclone center minimum.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original November 19–21 6-hour central-pressure/intensity timeline with a November 20 1801Z satellite position.

alternate_reviews.title: Australian forecasters issue the first full cyclone warning ahead of Tracy
alternate_reviews.location: Tiwi Islands and waters north of Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia
alternate_reviews.verified_core_fact: On December 22, 1974, the Darwin Tropical Cyclone Warning Centre issued a full cyclone warning for the Tiwi Islands as Cyclone Tracy was tracked north of Darwin.
alternate_reviews.source_independence_assessment: The Bureau of Meteorology historical operational warning chronology dates the first full warning about 24 hours after a December 21 formation alert; National Archives independently preserves Tracy's larger storm history but cites Bureau reports for this timing.
alternate_reviews.unverified_claims: Tracy's tropical depression was identified December 20, first formation alert December 21, full cyclone warning December 22, and catastrophic Darwin passage Christmas Day December 25. Do not place the Darwin destruction on December 22.
alternate_reviews.graphic_concept: Original December 20–25 warning/track timeline with the Tiwi Islands first full cyclone warning highlighted.

editorial_deferrals.reason: Both original unverified fog county leads discarded. Selected separate episodes: 1926 Utah avalanche and 1962 Hamburg coastal surge. The latter is an early February 17 Hamburg local peak following February 16 winds.

Fort McMurray May 11 is a dated *continued emergency bulletin*, not first ignition or the satellite acquisition date (May 6). Source-supported alternative still carries narrative/anniversary quality warning.
Hurricane Emily's Category 5 was analyzed at 0000 UTC July 17, which remains late July 16 on Caribbean local time; don't silently shift dates or claim a July 17 local landfall.
Hurricane Kate intensified to 953 hPa on November 20 but made landfall November 21. Aircraft/buoy pressures have independent-sensor differences and best-track estimates.
Cyclone Tracy first detection was Dec 20, formation alert Dec 21, full Tiwi Islands warning Dec 22, Darwin's destructive passage Dec 25; avoid misleading landfall caption.
